svg.data-asic: Broadcom Jericho2 BCM88690 with Broadcom OP2 BCM16K external TCAM
svg.data-timing: Stratum 3E OCXO with optional holdover; SyncE (ITU-T); IEEE 1588v2 default, G.8265.1, G.8275.1, G.8275.2, SMPTE ST 2059-2 (additional licence), T-GM, T-BC/OC, T-TC; Time Sensitive Networking (TSN); Class C timing accuracy. NOS integration is required to activate these, which the datasheet states with an asterisk against the whole timing block
svg.data-gnss: internal receiver for master clock implementations
svg.data-coherent: 400G ZR and OpenZR+ on the six 100/400G QSFP-DD, OpenZR+ on the eight 40/100G QSFP-DD - the capability the platform is named for
svg.data-optics-sfp-plus: 10G on the two SFP+ management ports. The datasheet's Compatible Transceiver Types list names QSFP-DD, QSFP56 and QSFP28 optics only and no SFP+ part at all, so the speed here is the port list's ('2 x 10G SFP+ management ports') and no specific module is claimed for it
svg.data-compliance-programme: IEEE 802.1CM fronthaul; ITU-T G.8273.2 T-BC Class C
svg.data-console: RJ45 RS-232 plus a micro-USB serial console
svg.data-timing-interfaces: GNSS SMA in; 1PPS SMB in/out; 10MHz SMB in/out; ToD RJ45 in/out; BITS RJ48 in/out
svg.data-emc: FCC Part 15, Subpart B, Class A; ICES-003, Class A; EN 55032, Class A; EN 300 386; EN 55035; EN 301 489; EN 303 413; EN 62479; EN 50663; VCCI CISPR 32, Class A

That is a stronger silence than the sibling guides', which table the system and FRU lamps and only omit the ports. Every lamp on this device therefore keeps its component's off/on default. The two lamps beside each QSFP28 pair and the one on each QSFP-DD light-pipe strip are drawn because the photograph and Figure 8 both show them; what they mean is not stated anywhere.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["qsfp28","qsfpdd-100g","qsfpdd-400g","port-leds"],"wanted":"a per-NOS LED table from UfiSpace or a NOS vendor, or photographs of a live unit with ports in known states","what":"port-led-semantics"},{"note":"Section 10 of this guide verifies system operation without a single LED table, so the six front-panel lamps (which the photograph shows as five green and one blue), the PSU lamp and the fan lamp have no published vocabulary. The S9500-30XS and S9510-28DC guides table theirs, and the temptation is to borrow: that is not done here, because those are different platforms and a borrowed table would read in the manifest exactly like a sourced one. The legend block's row order - SYNC, SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1, ID - is read off the artwork, not off a table.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["status-leds","psus","fans"],"wanted":"a section 10 with LED tables in a later HIG revision, or a NOS state map","what":"fru-led-semantics"},{"note":"The HIG Component Physical Information table gives the fan module 81 x 113 x 81.5 mm. HIG Figure 7's rear elevation puts two independent repeated features - the airflow tag and the status lamp - on an 84.4 mm pitch across the four modules, so the repeating unit is 84.4 and the visible face is that less a small web. The manifest carries an 82.5 mm face on an 84.4 mm pitch. This is the third UfiSpace fan in the library to show the same split, and the likely resolution is the same one: 81 measures the fan BODY behind a wider flange. That is an inference and neither document says it.","reason":"sources-disagree","scope":["ufispace/fan-803816@1","fans"],"wanted":"a vendor mechanical drawing of FAN-803816, or a caliper on the FRU","what":"fan-face-width"},{"note":"No held figure of the rear passes an aspect gate. HIG Figure 7 draws the chassis top surface in perspective above the rear face, so its bounding box measures 4.217 against a true 4.9715 and its vertical scale cannot be taken directly. The face was anchored instead on the PSU stack, whose 40 mm height the HIG states, which fixes the scale but not the origin better than about a millimetre. Every vertical number on the rear - the fan bay top and height, the PSU bay tops - therefore carries about ten times the uncertainty of the front, where the photograph passed the gate at 0.3%.","reason":"needs-drawing","scope":["rear","fans","psus"],"wanted":"a dimensioned rear elevation, or an orthographic rear photograph","what":"rear-vertical-scale"},{"note":"The HIG has a whole section on replacing an air filter (Figure 42) and the filter is not modelled, because no held figure shows where it sits on a face. Figure 42 draws the filter being drawn out of the chassis in three-quarter view without establishing which face it enters, and the front and rear elevations show no filter frame. A part with a replacement procedure is a part, not decoration - so its absence here is a missing component and not a decision.","reason":"needs-photo","scope":["rear"],"wanted":"a figure or photograph locating the air filter's access on a face","what":"air-filter"},{"note":"The C20 identification for the AC supply's inlet rests on the drawn three-slot pattern in HIG Figure 7 and on the datasheet's 200-240 V 10 A input, not on a stated cord type: unlike the S9311-64D's guide, which names 'IEC60320 C19', this one never names the cord anywhere. A C19 cord and a C20 inlet are the natural reading at 1600 W, and the drawn aperture measures 19.6 x 36.5 against the registry's 24.4 x 32.4 rotated cutout, which is close but not exact.","reason":"needs-photo","scope":["ufispace/psu-162-ac@1","psus"],"wanted":"a close-up photograph of the PSU-162 inlet, or a cord type in a later revision","what":"ac-inlet-standard"},{"note":"No held figure shows a DC build seated in the chassis. HIG Figure 7 and every product render show the AC unit with its appliance inlet, and the guide's DC section illustrates cable routing rather than the faceplate, so the DC contract carries the AC unit's measured face with a two-post terminal block substituted on the inlet's footprint. The datasheet rates the DC input at -40 to -72 V and 50 A, which is a stud-and-lug interface rather than a coupler, but its geometry is inferred.","reason":"needs-drawing","scope":["ufispace/psu-162-dc@1","psus"],"wanted":"a rear photograph or elevation of a DC-configured S9600-30DX","what":"dc-psu-face"},{"note":"No held document prints an orderable chassis part number - the datasheet and the HIG name the product only as S9600-30DX, and the Available to Order block names only the two PSUs and one fan. The datasheet mentions 'an external TCAM option' and a memory range without naming SKUs for either. The S9510-28DC precedent applies: that model's SKUs surfaced from the owner and from no held PDF, so the configurations carry no part-numbers rather than invented ones.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["base","ac","dc"],"wanted":"a UfiSpace ordering guide, or the TCAM and memory option SKUs","what":"chassis-sku"}],"groups":{"fans":{"description":"the four rear fans, which the rear panel numbers 0 to 3","index-origin":0,"role":"service","term":"Fan"},"furniture":{"index-origin":1,"role":"furniture","term":"Item"},"grounding":{"index-origin":1,"role":"furniture","term":"Point"},"mgmt":{"index-origin":1,"mixed":"the management block down the left edge - the out-of-band RJ45, the RS-232 console RJ45, the micro-USB serial console, the USB 2.0 service port and the recessed reset button","role":"management","term":"Port"},"port-leds":{"description":"every indicator that belongs to a particular port - two lamps on the green band beside each QSFP28 pair and one on the light pipe beside each QSFP-DD column","index-origin":1,"role":"indicator","term":"LED"},"psus":{"index-origin":0,"role":"service","term":"PSU"},"qsfp28":{"attrs":{"media":"qsfp28","speed":"100g"},"description":"ports 0-15, the datasheet's '16 x 40/100G QSFP28 ports', in four columns of two stacked pairs. Numbering runs DOWN each column, which is why port 1 sits under port 0 rather than beside it","index-origin":0,"role":"traffic","term":"Port"},"qsfpdd-100g":{"attrs":{"media":"qsfp-dd","speed":"100g"},"description":"ports 16-23, the datasheet's '8 x 40/100G QSFP-DD ports with OpenZR+ support', the four columns the faceplate marks with gold-olive light pipes","index-origin":0,"role":"traffic","term":"Port"},"qsfpdd-400g":{"attrs":{"media":"qsfp-dd","speed":"400g"},"description":"ports 24-29, the datasheet's '6 x 100/400G QSFP-DD ports with 400G ZR/ZR+ support', the three columns the faceplate marks with blue light pipes - the coherent uplinks the platform is named for","index-origin":0,"role":"traffic","term":"Port"},"sfp-plus":{"attrs":{"media":"sfp-plus","speed":"10g"},"description":"the stacked SFP+ pair at the left of the faceplate, numbered 0 and 1 in their own run - the datasheet's '2 x 10G SFP+ management ports'","index-origin":0,"role":"management","term":"Port"},"status-leds":{"description":"the six chassis indicators the faceplate legends SYNC, SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1 and ID - five green and one blue beacon, with no published vocabulary","index-origin":1,"role":"indicator","term":"LED"},"timing":{"index-origin":1,"mixed":"the timing block at the right of the faceplate - a GNSS antenna on SMA, 1PPS and 10MHz on SMB, ToD on RJ45 and BITS on RJ48. Four media, five jacks, one job: this is the block that makes an aggregation router a Class C grandmaster","role":"management","term":"Port"}},"kind":"device","manufacturer":"UfiSpace","maturity":"modelled","model":"S9600-30DX","name":"s9600-30dx","provenance":{"attrs":"datasheet - Specifications, Performance, Environmental, Regulatory Compliance and Accessories sections, transcribed into sections. Compliance strings kept verbatim, semicolon-separated, untidied.","chassis":"datasheet - 'Chassis (W x D x H) 2RU, 436 x 762 x 87.7 mm', weight 20.62 kg without FRU; the HIG Component Physical Information table repeats the same triple and the same weight. 436 is the body and not a rack face: the HIG's Space Clearance section says 'The S9600-30DX width is 17.16 inches (43.6cm) and shipped with a rack mount brackets suitable for 19 inch (48.3cm) wide racks', so the mounting hardware is additional to 436 and is not drawn. 762 mm is the chassis without FRUs; the same section projects the fan handles 29 mm and the PSU handles 30 mm beyond it.","grounding":"HIG section 8 - the grounding lug bolts to the rear face, on the chassis strip between the fan bank and the PSU stack. Figure 7 draws a silver two-hole plate there with an earth symbol beside it, and HIG Figure 4's overview calls it out by name ('Ground Lug') with a leader to that exact strip. The DC build ships five lugs and the AC build one (HIG accessory list), which is why the DC configuration says so.","left-cluster":"drawing - measured on the photograph at 3.59 px/mm and cross-read against HIG Figure 8 at 7x. Down the left edge: a white six-row legend block with its lamp column BESIDE it (x 15.87-18.65, six lamps on a 2.44 mm pitch from y 25.53 to 39.13 - five green and one blue, the ID beacon), a reset pinhole below it, then the micro-USB console and a portrait USB-A. To their right, the stacked SFP+ management pair (apertures x 23.11-37.03, centres y 19.71 and 34.83 - on the same 15.13 mm grid as the traffic ports) over the stacked console and out-of-band RJ45 pair (x 22.83-35.92, centres y 53.01 and 67.30, a 14.29 mm pitch). std/rj45-ganged (12.7 x 11.0) is used rather than common/rj45-bezel@2 (17.0 x 14.9) because a 17 mm part cannot sit on a 14.29 mm pitch.","lifecycle":"searched 2026-08-28: the vendor's own product page was fetched and read for a notice, and none appears - the page is live and carries active downloads. none-announced is a real finding, not an absence.","port-numbers":"drawing - printed on the panel and drawn here. The QSFP28 numbers sit on the green label band outside each stacked pair, flanked by an up and a down triangle and two lamps; the QSFP-DD numbers sit on the light-pipe strip beside each column, the even one level with the upper aperture and the odd one with the lower. Both are visible on the metal in the photograph with the cages empty, which is what distinguishes them from HIG Figure 8's numerals - those are printed on the schematic module faces, where a seated module would cover them.","power":"datasheet 'Typical power: 464 Watts (no transceiver)' - the vendor's own scope, so power-envelope is bare. The HIG states the maximum twice, once per build: 'The maximum system power consumption is 1300 watts' in the AC section and '1276 watts' in the DC section, neither qualified as to optics or ambient. 1300 is carried as power-max-w because max means the highest, and the 24-watt difference is recorded here rather than as a conflict - they are two builds, not two readings. The 1600 W that appears beside them is a provisioning instruction ('a reserve of at least 1600 watts on each power circuit') and is the supply's rating, not a draw. On a single 110 VAC feed the HIG derates both supplies to 1000 W each. These are the vendor's figures as the vendor states them and are NOT reconciled against the module set; the fans publish no draw, so any total built from the modelled modules is a floor.","qsfp28-layout":"drawing - four columns, each a pair of 2-high stacked cages: one band spanning grid rows 1-2 and another spanning rows 3-4. Aperture runs measure 43.43-62.09, 66.82-85.47, 90.21-108.86 and 113.59-132.25 mm, all 18.66 wide on a 23.39 pitch, so common/qsfp-cage@2 (19.5) is centred on each at lefts 43.01 + 23.39k. NUMBERING RUNS DOWN EACH COLUMN, not across the row: the green label band above the upper pair reads '\u25b2 0 \u2299\u2299 1 \u25bc', '\u25b2 2 \u2299\u2299 3 \u25bc' and so on, so column k carries ports 2k over 2k+1 in the upper band and 8+2k over 9+2k in the lower. Read at 5x off the photograph and confirmed against HIG Figure 8, which prints 0 2 4 6 across its upper row and 1 3 5 7 beneath - the same assignment stated the other way round.","qsfpdd-layout":"drawing - seven columns on grid rows 2 and 3, in four pair-slots separated by light-pipe strips. The strips are the ruler and they are unambiguous in colour: gold-olive at x 138.93, 182.36, 188.49 and 231.92 bounding the eight OpenZR+ ports, blue at 237.77, 281.20, 287.33 and 311.65 bounding the six 400G ZR ports. Between them the cages measure 19.49, 19.49, 19.21 and 19.21 mm - the QSFP-DD faceplate opening to a fifth of a millimetre - so std/qsfp-dd sits at lefts 143.63, 163.12, 193.19, 212.68, 242.89, 262.10 and 292.45. Column j carries port 16+2j over 17+2j, which puts 16-23 in the OpenZR+ group and 24-29 in the ZR group exactly as the datasheet's two rows split them.","rear-layout":"drawing, and WEAKER THAN THE FRONT - said plainly because the difference matters. HIG Figure 7's rear elevation (fig-0012) draws the chassis's top surface in perspective above the rear face, so the panel's own bounding box fails the aspect gate at 4.217 against a true 4.9715 and cannot set the vertical scale. The horizontal scale is the panel width (1358 px = 436 mm, 3.115 px/mm) and on it the four fan modules repeat cleanly: the airflow tag sits on an 84.44 mm pitch and the status lamp on 84.33, agreeing to a tenth of a millimetre. Vertically the face was anchored on the PSU stack, whose 40 mm height the HIG states, giving a face top at py 56. Fan bay origin and the PSU block's left edge are read off that frame and are good to about a millimetre, not the third of a millimetre the front carries.","row-grid":"drawing - ALL FOUR PORT ROWS SIT ON ONE GRID, and that is a measurement rather than a tidying. Profiling a column strictly inside a QSFP28 cage gives four aperture bands centred at 20.26 / 35.52 / 50.23 / 65.64 mm - intervals of 15.26, 14.71 and 15.41, a spread of 0.7 mm on a 15.13 mm mean, which is noise at 3.6 px/mm. Profiling a QSFP-DD column gives its two apertures centred at 35.94 and 50.10, within 0.4 mm of grid rows 2 and 3. The two blocks are therefore laid out on the same centrelines and are modelled that way; the alternative is a half-millimetre stagger between neighbouring blocks that no source asserts.","scale-gate":"TWO SOURCES PASS THE GATE AND THE PHOTOGRAPH WINS, which is unusual enough to say plainly. HIG Figure 8's port overview (fig-0013) measures 1398 x 284 px against the stated 436 x 87.7 mm chassis - aspect 4.923 against a true 4.9715, 1.0% out - so it is orthographic and carries geometry. But the second product render measures 1566 x 316 px, aspect 4.956, 0.3% out, at 3.5917 px/mm across and 3.6032 down: a third better in aspect and a tenth better in resolution than the guide figure, and it draws the cages EMPTY where the figure draws them with modules seated over the numbers. The front geometry here is therefore measured on the PHOTOGRAPH and confirmed against the figure, which inverts this project's usual order and is only legitimate because the photograph passed the same aspect gate the figure did. Where the two disagree they disagree by under a millimetre; the port-block ends agree to 0.4 mm across 270 mm.","sources":"UfiSpace S9600-30DX datasheet (working/intake/ufispace/converted/s9600-30dx-datasheet) for dimensions, weight, port inventory, platform, timing, power, environment, compliance and the FRU ordering lines; S9600-30DX Hardware Installation Guide (s9600-30dx-hig) for the overview, port and fan figures, the FRU dimension table, the maximum-power and space-clearance sentences and grounding; three vendor product renders (photos/s9600-30dx-1-view, -2-view, -3-view - unlabelled, identified by aspect and content) for the front face, colour and counts. Checked for a vendor 3D model before trusting any figure, per the skill: the intake stages GLBs for ReadyLinks only and none for UfiSpace.","timing-block":"drawing/datasheet - and the media are NOT the family's. The datasheet is explicit that GNSS is SMA while 1PPS and 10MHz are SMB ('1 x GNSS input SMA, 1 x 10MHz input/output SMB, 1 x 1PPS input/output SMB'), which is the S9510-28DC's split and the opposite of the S9500-30XS's all-SMA block - the reason for measuring rather than assuming the family shape. The drawn sizes agree: 1PPS and 10MHZ measure 4.05 mm across the nut and GNSS ANT 10.02, at x 371.76, 386.73 and 401.90, all on y 36.75. BITS and TOD are side by side rather than stacked, apertures x 327.42-340.22 and 347.46-360.27 on y 29.70-40.24. The GNSS jack is ROUND: common/sma-jack draws a hex nut, which is the S9510-28DC's hardware and not this one's, so it is std/sma on a gold decor disc - the same construction the S9311-64D and S9500-30XS needed.","views":"Six views. TOP: y = 0 is the REAR, per the house convention and HIG Figure 4's footprint drawing, which prints the fan handles at the top edge; five long stadium recesses run across the lid, proportioned off that drawing. BOTTOM carries the compliance sticker at an estimated position - no held figure shows the underside. LEFT (x = 0 is the REAR) and RIGHT (x = 0 is the FRONT) carry the rail screws the HIG's rack-mounting section describes, at estimated positions; both side faces otherwise carry only symmetric content, so the depth-axis conventions are stated here rather than exposed by any asymmetric feature. This chassis also has a replaceable air filter (HIG section 'Replacing the Air Filter', Figure 42) which is NOT modelled - see the air-filter gap."},"references":[{"title":"UfiSpace S9600-30DX Hardware Installation Guide"}],"version":"0.1.0","views":{"bottom":{"components":{"placements":[{"at":[108.0,280.0],"group":"furniture","id":"bottom-label","ref":"common/compliance-sticker@1","rel-pos":1}]},"size":{"h":762,"w":436}},"front":{"components":{"placements":[{"at":[6.9,37.6],"for":"chassis","group":"mgmt","id":"reset","ref":"common/reset-button@1","rel-pos":5},{"at":[16.5,25.09],"description":"Legended SYNC on the faceplate. The S9600-30DX HIG publishes no LED table of any kind, so the states are the component default rather than a vocabulary borrowed from a sibling guide - see the fru-led-semantics
